frameworks.name: DSO Consolidation Formula
frameworks.definition: A multi-practice dental acquisition model that pools 4-5 independent practices into a unified dental support organization (DSO) under shared ownership, enabling higher valuation multiples and improved unit economics through consolidated buying power and operational leverage.

frameworks.name: Multi-Tier Offer Waterfall
frameworks.definition: An acquisition offer structure that provides clear tier levels (e.g., 4x multiple for solo practice, 7x for participation in DSO, 10-12x for consolidated platform), with founders keeping equity above the baseline to incentivize participation.

frameworks.name: IP Carve-Out Strategy
frameworks.definition: Separating intellectual property (coaching curriculum, AI portal, systems) from the core operational business being sold, with the IP retained as a separate entity and licensed back to the acquirer under defined terms and territories.

claims.text: A wellness dentistry practice generating $4M revenue with an associated coaching platform generating $1M can achieve a $100M valuation in approximately 3 years by consolidating 4-5 practices into a DSO structure, because higher EBITDA multiples (10-12x vs. 4x for solo practices) multiply unit economics when combined with effective operations consolidation.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Wellness dentistry niche with 20% EBITDA margins
Existing coaching client base for acquisition pipeline
Ability to consolidate 4-5 practices operationally
claims.mechanism: Higher acquisition multiples (10-12x DSO vs 4x solo) apply to consolidated EBITDA; at $10M+ EBITDA, this multiplier compounds into 8-figure valuations within 3-year consolidation window.
bounded_by: Requires operational consolidation, not just financial stacking
Assumes stable 20%+ EBITDA margins maintained post-consolidation

claims.text: When acquiring independent practices into a DSO, structure the offer with a baseline multiple (e.g., 7x) that exceeds solo-practice market multiples (4x), with the incremental gain above the baseline (e.g., 10x total minus 7x baseline = 3x retained) kept as founder upside to incentivize participation and reduce holdout risk.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Consolidating peer practices (4-5 units)
Targeting EBITDA multiples in 4-12x range
First consolidation to establish proof of concept
claims.mechanism: Offering founders 7x (vs 4x available solo) anchors their expectation above current market, while retaining incremental upside (3-5x additional) creates psychological commitment and aligns incentives with achieving consolidated platform value.

numbers.axis: Acquisition offer structure by valuation tier

bounded_by: Requires capital to fund the 7x baseline for initial participants
Does not apply to distressed sellers or those with immediate liquidity needs

claims.text: The coaching and educational platform is the strategic asset that generates the deal pipeline (prospect practices approach for scaling help), so it must be retained as a separate entity post-acquisition, with the IP licensed back to the consolidated DSO operations rather than sold alongside the practices.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Coach-built advisory model with recurring client relationships
IP includes proprietary systems, checklists, protocols, and AI tools
Exit target is a DSO roll-up rather than sale of entire platform
claims.mechanism: The coaching business is the goose (asset that generates repeating deal flow); the practice acquisitions are the eggs (outputs). Selling the eggs while keeping the goose means founders retain the repeating revenue stream and can leverage it to acquire successive cohorts of practices.
bounded_by: Only applies if coaching business has demonstrable track record and standalone unit economics
Requires acquirer acceptance of IP licensing terms (unlimited use for X period/territory)

claims.text: Consolidating multiple independent practices into a DSO operationally accomplishes 75% of the integration work that would otherwise occur post-acquisition, so founders can begin the process during the pre-acquisition scaling phase by standardizing systems, pricing, training, and operations across prospect practices.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Consolidation occurs pre-acquisition, not post-purchase
Founders retain operational control and systems definition authority
Prospect practices have voluntary participation (coaching clients)
claims.mechanism: Early integration of operations reduces acquisition integration friction and post-purchase surprises; the acquirer inherits a systems-aligned, unified operating model rather than fragmented practices requiring expensive post-acquisition restructuring.
bounded_by: Applies only to founder-controlled consolidations, not to purchased acquisitions without owner buy-in

claims.text: To prevent holdout behavior from individual practice owners during a multi-unit DSO exit, require all participating practices to agree in writing upfront to drag-along rights and 100% business acquisition rights, giving the lead founder unilateral authority to execute sales above a negotiated threshold without requiring unanimous consent.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Multi-practice consolidation (4+ units)
Exit to private equity or strategic buyer
Deal value exceeds agreed threshold
claims.mechanism: Drag-along rights prevent the last holdout from extracting supernormal rent from other shareholders at close; without pre-agreed rights, rational behavior diverges between individual parties (hold out for premium) and platform value (close on time).
bounded_by: Requires all participants to accept terms before consolidation begins
May be limited by state law or company structure (S-corp vs. LLC considerations)

claims.text: The wellness dentistry niche is defensible via premium positioning because it addresses a motivated buyer archetype (patients seeking biological, holistic dental care aligned with overall wellness), enabling higher pricing and margins than mass-market dentistry.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Niche focus: biological and holistic dentistry modality
Patient avatar explicitly seeking wellness alignment
Educational differentiation via coaching platform
claims.mechanism: Niche buyers are willing to pay premium prices for services aligned with their explicit values; the wellness coaching platform reinforces the positioning by adding educational and accountability services, making the core dental service a higher-value package.
bounded_by: Positioning is defensible only if practice consistently delivers on wellness claims

claims.text: A DSO acquisition offer that appears to offer only a 7x multiple can simultaneously look attractive and contain 3-5x hidden upside by clarifying that the 7x reflects consolidated platform value (10-12x) minus individual practice baseline (4x), making the founder feel they are capturing 75% of the consolidated gain without requiring significant additional capital from the acquirer.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Offering to early participants in consolidation
Comparing against available solo-practice alternatives (4x)
Structuring upside as vesting or earn-out rather than downpayment
claims.mechanism: Anchoring founders' expectations against their realistic solo-practice alternative (4x) makes a 7x offer appear to capture 75% of the 3x platform premium, even though the acquirer retains option rights to the remaining upside; psychological commitment is secured by transparent communication of the multiple structure.

numbers.axis: Founder perceived capture of consolidation value

bounded_by: Transparency must be explicit; founders perceiving 7x as final offer will resist

claims.text: A coaching platform built on proprietary IP (systems, checklists, protocols, AI tools, and training curriculum) creates a sustainable competitive moat and ongoing deal pipeline because prospective practice-owner clients are already invested in the methodology and trust the founder, making them natural acquisition targets for consolidation.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Coaching clients have ongoing paid relationships with the founder
Clients are practice owners operating in the same niche (wellness dentistry)
IP is proprietary and difficult to replicate
claims.mechanism: Existing coaching relationships establish baseline trust and reduce acquisition friction; founders already know the prospect's business, challenges, and values, lowering due diligence costs and increasing close rate relative to cold acquisition targets.
bounded_by: Only applies when coaching business has >2 years track record and strong retention

examples.text: A wellness dentistry practice owner with $4M revenue and a $1M coaching platform approached consolidation by identifying 4-5 existing coaching clients (other practice owners they had worked with for years) as acquisition targets. The acquirer recognized the deal structure as attractive because the consolidation would enable higher valuation multiples (10-12x vs. 4x solo), would unify operations and systems before the acquisition closed, and would preserve the coaching platform as a repeating asset for future consolidations.

A dentistry DSO deal was structured by Alex Hormozi with drag-along rights and 100% acquisition rights negotiated upfront among all five participating practices. This mechanism prevented any single practice owner from becoming a holdout during the exit and enabled unanimous agreement on sale timing and terms. The mechanism required all parties to accept the terms before consolidation began, not after valuations increased.

practices.text: When consolidating multiple independent practices toward a future DSO exit, negotiate and document drag-along rights and 100% business acquisition rights upfront from all participating parties to prevent holdout behavior at close.

Separate the coaching/educational IP from the core operational business in all acquisition discussions; license it back to the consolidated DSO under defined terms rather than selling it as part of the exit.

Frame acquisition offers to early consolidation participants by comparing them against realistic solo-practice alternatives (e.g., 4x multiples), not against the final platform value, to anchor founder expectations and secure psychological commitment.
Standardize systems, pricing, training, and operations across practices during the pre-acquisition consolidation phase to reduce post-acquisition integration costs and complexity.
